summary: Explored operator's proposal to use native .NET Task APIs for automatic promotion of long-running Jarvis tool calls to jobs. Confirmed Task.WhenAny(operation, Task.Delay(threshold)) is the clean fast/pending branch and does not cancel the original task; Task.WaitAsync(timeout) similarly leaves underlying task running but throws TimeoutException rather than representing pending; CancellationTokenSource.CancelAfter is for cancellation not promotion. Proposed registered Task<AgentCommandResponse> job handle, bounded operation admission, 3-second fast path, late-result polling through server-side store while underlying client command continues. Inspected production Jarvis source: existing Client.JobManager stores OS Processes, stdout/stderr events (up to 100 completed), not arbitrary task outcomes; Server/McpTools.send awaits ClientService.SendCommandToUser; ClientService reads HttpContext.RequestAborted, uses it in SendCommand/Tracking waits, and Server/Program.fs registers ClientService as scoped, while ClientResponseTracker is singleton. Therefore naive detached task capturing scoped ClientService/HttpContext will be canceled/invalid when original HTTP request completes. Need independent background lifetime, copied authenticated routing identity, operation ID, bounded queue, own timeout/cancellation and result registry; process JobResult has different shape from tool response, so extend jobs as typed union or separate operation jobs. Keep original AgentCommandResponse (errors, instructions, state changes) for final result; pending state does not imply agentStateChanges=[] because effects still unknown. Task.WhenAny is only the response promotion mechanism, not a fix for synchronous SignalR client handler head-of-line blocking, nor does it make server-memory jobs durable across restarts. Read official Microsoft docs for Task.WhenAny, Task.WaitAsync, ASP.NET hosted queues/background HttpContext safety. No source/task modifications or deployment. Lead yielding Ready.
nextAction: Operator: no further action required for design exploration. If approving implementation, refine existing P2 task task-b0e62987fa03497a809a7d1bdd700ae4 around Task.WhenAny fast path and server-owned generic ToolJob registry with bounded execution/lifetime, independent authenticated status polling and exact operation-ID/reconciliation behavior; independently reproduce/fix SignalR receive-loop head-of-line blocking. Consider separate response schema for generic tool jobs instead of treating them as Process JobResult.
